In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new class of antitumor agents based on the structural modification of the 2,4,6-triaminopyrimidines.
the design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a series of 2,4-diaryl-6-alkylpyrimidines (benzoprims) and their derivatives, which are potent inhibitors of dihydrofolate-reductase.
the development of a novel class of DHFR inhibitors, the benzoprims, which are potent antitumor agents in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these compounds do not have the potential to inhibit DHFR and that the benzoprim structure is essential for DHFR inhibition.
the nitrobenzylamidines 1,2,4,6,8 and 9 are potent inhibitors of DHFR but the benzimidazole-N-oxides 10,12,13,16,18 and 19 are not.
the benzoprim N-oxide series is not likely to be useful for anti-ras therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benzoprim series is a potent and highly selective inhibitor of DHFR, but that the benzimidazole N-oxide modification does not abrogate the activity of these inhibitors.

the introduction of the benzimidazole-N-oxides into the lipophilic benzoprim series has resulted in a loss of growth-inhibitory activity, but that these new compounds have retained some DHFR-inhibiting potency and have shown no evidence of anti-ras activity.

benzoprim N-oxide 4a was a potent DHFR inhibitor but was inactive against the two human cell lines tested; benzoprim N-methyl-oxime 5a was also an effective DHFR inhibitor but had a weak antiproliferative activity (GI(50), 10 microM), while 4b was a weak DHFR inhibitor and had a low antiproliferation activity (GI(90), 50 microM).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the benzimidazole-N-oxides are not significantly more lipophilic than the parent compounds (e.g., logP values of 2.8 and 4.1 for methylbenzopim and the methylbenzopirin N-oxide 3, respectively) and that, as with methylbenzoprin, the benzimidazole N-oxide derivatives are not significantly more stable in the presence of human serum.
the benzimidazole-N-oxides 3-7 and 9-13 are not likely to have anti-ras activity.
the nitrophenyloxy group of 1 and 2 is a key structural component of DHFR-inhibition and, as such, cannot be replaced by other substituents.
